articles.title: Letter: Thanks to the Eastgate Senior Lunch Program
body: To the editor: Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.

Please keep the streetlight upgrade in the budget. Many of us on Quincy Place use it every week. To the editor: I have lived on Quincy Place for 9 years, and I want to say what a difference the Eastgate Senior Lunch Program has made.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the June meeting.
Dolores Orchard, Lower Millrace

articles.title: Zoning Board Hears Plan for Free Tax Clinic Near Foundry Row
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Keystone Street disagreed about cost and timing.
body: The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
Councilmember Zelda Donnelly asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $48,000.

Residents of Foundry Row said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street. Public works estimates the work will take about 15 weeks once it starts in October.

articles.title: Roman Lindqvist, 88, Parish Bookkeeper
articles.deck: Friends remember Roman Lindqvist for the many years of service to Foxglove Heights.
body: Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Foxglove Heights. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Lower Millrace Improvement Group in his or her name.
Born in Foxglove Heights in the years after the war, Roman Lindqvist spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Roman Lindqvist died in June at home on Hollis Place, at the age of 88.
